rv.q: Combined with energetic performances, convincing fight choreography, and a compelling central story, the production succeeds in delivering a heartfelt tribute to wrestling culture while remaining accessible to audiences unfamiliar with the sport.

Ultimately, wrestling fans may enjoy elements of this production, which draws so much from that medium’s tone and style, but theatergoers in search of a compelling plot or rich character development should look elsewhere.
The hype of the wrestling matches alone makes Two Out of Three Falls worth a watch.
This is a play that I can highly—and heartily—recommend.

That it comes out on top as a pretty good play is a boon in itself, but at the tail end of a season spent in awe of the delightfully twisty work being presented here at the Factory's home on Howard Street, is "a pretty good play" enough? Let's set the scene, though; something is rotten in the state of Texas.

cn.t: Wrestling drama explores grief and legacy through a daughter haunted by her father's ghost, but critics are split—some appreciate the emotional kayfabe, while others find the plot lightweight and underwhelming.
